_meta.indication: MEPSEVII is indicated in pediatric and adult patients for the treatment of Mucopolysaccharidosis VII (MPS VII, Sly syndrome).

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3 multicenter, randomized delayed (blind) start trial; 12 patients divided into four cohorts based on placebo exposure of 0, 8, 16 or 24 weeks before crossing over to 4 mg/kg vestronidase alfa infusions.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients diagnosed with MPS VII aged 5 to 35 years; the 12 enrolled ranged in age from 8 to 25 years (median 14), 4 male and 8 female, 75% white, 50% Hispanic or Latino.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: For US regulatory purposes no pre-specified primary endpoint was declared; efficacy was based on the totality of the clinical data on a per-subject basis (with a Multi-Domain Responder Index and 6MWT among the endpoints). Percent reduction in urinary GAG (dermatan sulfate) was the EU primary and a US secondary endpoint.
pivotal_trials.n: N=12 (3 immediate MEPSEVII, 3 placebo 8 wk, 3 placebo 16 wk, 3 placebo 24 wk before crossover)
pivotal_trials.result: After 24 weeks the LS mean difference in 6MWT between MEPSEVII and placebo was approximately 18 meters (SE 33); all patients were responders for uGAG (dermatan sulfate) with >=50% reduction, and urinary GAGs were maintained at approximately 60% to 80% reduction from baseline. The statistical team concluded no substantial evidence of efficacy; approval was based on the totality of evidence.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=1 patient) were infusion site extravasation, diarrhea, rash, anaphylaxis, infusion site swelling, peripheral swelling, and pruritus. Anaphylaxis, the most serious risk, occurred in 2 of 20 patients in the clinical program.
target_moa: Vestronidase alfa is a recombinant human beta-glucuronidase (rhGUS) enzyme replacement therapy identical in amino acid sequence to native human GUS; it carries mannose-6-phosphate residues that facilitate cell-surface receptor binding and internalization, and it reduces accumulated urinary glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) in patients with MPS VII who are deficient in beta-glucuronidase activity.
modality: enzyme (recombinant human beta-glucuronidase enzyme replacement therapy)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: ANAPHYLAXIS – Anaphylaxis has occurred with MEPSEVII administration, as early as the first dose; appropriate medical support should be readily available, patients closely observed during and for 60 minutes after infusion, and the infusion immediately discontinued if anaphylaxis occurs.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee was not convened during the review of BLA 761047.

summary.text: MEPSEVII (vestronidase alfa-vjbk) received Orphan Drug designation (Feb 16, 2012) and Fast Track designation (July 15, 2015) for enzyme replacement therapy in MPS VII, was granted priority review, and the sponsor received a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.
